notes.meaning: We should not lose our temper or become jealous when evil people seem to succeed. Their prosperity is only temporary and will quickly fade. Fretting and burning with anger only leads us into trouble.
Wicked people will wither away just like green grass cut down under the hot sun. Their success in this life does not last long. We have no reason to envy someone whose glory vanishes so quickly.

Instead of worrying about what sinners have, we are told to place our confidence in the Lord and do good. God wants His people to stay faithful right where He places them. When we trust Him, He provides all the daily food and safety we need.

True joy comes from delighting in the Lord and enjoying His goodness. When our hearts are focused on Him, He shapes our wants so they match His holy will. He then gladly gives us what our renewed hearts truly long for.

Believers are encouraged to roll all their burdens, plans, and worries over to the Lord in prayer. When we completely depend on Him instead of our own strength, He works behind the scenes. He promises to accomplish everything needed for our good.

God will make your innocence and honesty shine out clearly for all to see. Even if your name is misunderstood or hidden in darkness for a season, the Lord will bring justice. In His perfect time, your upright character will be as obvious as the bright midday sun.

We are called to be still and wait calmly for the Lord instead of trying to take matters into our own hands. It can be hard to watch dishonest people carry out bad schemes and still get ahead. Patient silence shows we trust God to act at the right moment.

Letting anger burn inside us only damages our character and pushes us toward doing wrong. Fretting over evil people tempts us to copy their dishonest ways to get ahead. Turning away from rage keeps our hearts peaceful and obedient.

People who do evil will eventually be removed and cut off from God's blessings. Those who put their hope in the Lord, however, will receive the land He promised. God always keeps His promise to care for those who wait on Him.

The power of the ungodly lasts only a short moment. Soon they will be completely gone from the earth. Even if you search carefully for the places where they once ruled, you will find nothing left of them.

Lowly and gentle people who rely on God rather than pushing their own way will inherit the land. They enjoy true, abundant peace deep inside their hearts. Their simple trust in God gives them a satisfaction that worldly wealth can never buy.

Wicked people make secret plans to hurt those who follow God and grind their teeth in bitter anger against them. They despise the godly simply because the godly strive to do what is right. Their hatred cannot overcome the protection God gives His people.

The Lord is not worried by the threats of the wicked; He laughs at their foolish schemes. He already knows the exact day set for their judgment. No matter how powerful they appear now, their time of punishment is rushing toward them.

The ungodly draw out their swords and bend their bows to attack the poor and needy. They want to crush those who live upright, godly lives. Their cruelty aims directly at the people God loves and defends.

God turns the violent schemes of evildoers back upon their own heads. Their own swords will pierce their hearts, and the bows they use to harm others will snap. The Lord ensures that sin brings its own punishment.

The little that a righteous person owns is far better than the vast wealth of many wicked people. A modest meal with God's blessing brings quiet contentment and joy to the soul. Great riches gained without God bring only trouble, guilt, and fear of judgment.

The strength and power of ungodly people will be broken so they can no longer do harm. At the same time, the Lord Himself holds up the righteous by His own hand. God's mighty support is stronger than any earthly weapon.

The Lord watches over every single day and trouble in the lives of His blameless people. He knows what they need and cares for them through every trial. The spiritual inheritance He gives them will never fade and lasts forever.

When hard times fall upon the land, believers will not be left to shame or despair. Even during terrible famines, God provides enough to satisfy their needs. Those who trust Him can count on His daily faithfulness.

Those who oppose the Lord will perish quickly, like wildflowers that fade or like the fat of sacrifices burned on an altar. Their proud glory will vanish like a puff of smoke. When God's judgment comes, nothing of their worldly power will remain.

The wicked often sink into debt and fail to repay what they borrow, whether from greed or ruin. In contrast, righteous people are generous and quick to share because God has blessed them. True faith shows itself in open-handed kindness toward others.

Those who receive the Lord's blessing are promised a secure place in His land. But those who live under His curse will be completely destroyed. It is God's favor, not worldly force, that secures a lasting future.

The Lord makes firm every step of the person who walks in obedience to Him. God watches over their daily journey and takes great pleasure in their faithful path. His loving guidance gives believers true direction and stability.

A godly person may stumble into deep trials or sudden trouble, but they will not be destroyed. The Lord keeps a firm grip on their hand and catches them before they are ruined. His unfailing support keeps His children secure through every hardship.

differ.view: A true believer may fall into sin for a time. But God's grace brings him back to repentance, and he can never be finally lost.
The "fall" here means falling into trouble, not into sin. Believers stay safe as they keep trusting and obeying God.

notes.meaning: Looking back over a long life from youth to old age, the psalmist shares what he has seen. He never saw the faithful people of God truly deserted, nor their children reduced to begging for bread. God faithfully supplies the essential needs of those who honor Him.

Godly people are continually merciful and eager to lend to neighbors who are in need. Instead of running out of resources, their families are blessed by the Lord. A generous spirit brings God's favor down onto future generations.

Believers are told to walk away from all sin and actively practice what is good. Doing what is right leads to a secure dwelling place under God's loving protection. Turning from evil is the path to living with Him forever.

The Lord loves true justice and will never abandon those who belong to Him. He keeps His faithful saints safe forever, while cutting off the family line of the wicked. His loyalty to His people remains steady in every age.

The righteous will receive the land God promised them and live there forever. God gives His people a permanent home filled with peace and safety. His holy promises are sure and will never be taken away from them.

Righteous people fill their speech with godly wisdom and fair judgment. What they say comes from thinking deeply about God's truth. Their words offer helpful guidance and encouragement to those around them.

God's word is not just written on paper for the righteous person; it is planted deep in their heart. Because God's instructions guide their thoughts and choices, their feet walk steadily. Having God's truth on the inside keeps them from slipping into sin.

Wicked people keep a close watch on the righteous, waiting for any chance to attack or destroy them. They plot how to ruin the godly person's life and good name. Even when evil seems hidden, God sees every trap that is set.

The Lord will not abandon His servants to the mercy of their enemies or let unfair accusations stand against them. When human courts or slanderous voices condemn the innocent, God Himself acquits them. The Lord's final judgment overturns the harsh words of the world.

We are called to wait patiently on the Lord and keep walking in the way of His commands. When we stay faithful, He will lift us up to receive His promised blessings. You will outlast the schemes of evildoers and see justice done when they are removed.

The psalmist describes seeing a violent, wicked person who seemed full of power and influence. Like a leafy tree growing strong in its native soil, this man appeared secure and impossible to shake. Outward success often makes arrogant people look untouchable.

Yet in an instant that powerful sinner was gone, as if he had never existed. Even when someone went looking for him, not a trace of his glory could be found. Worldly power that ignores God disappears like a passing shadow.

Look closely at the person who lives an honest and blameless life before God. Even if their path has hardship, that man of peace will find a quiet and blessed future. Walking with the Lord always leads to lasting peace in the end.

differ.view: God can make a believer "perfect" in heart in this life, saving him from all sin and filling him with His love.
No one is perfect in themselves. Believers are counted perfect because they are joined to Christ.

notes.meaning: Those who stubbornly keep breaking God's law will face total ruin together. The future that wicked people hoped to build will be cut short. Disobedience leaves a person with no lasting hope or peace.

The deliverance and rescue of the righteous come entirely from the Lord, not from their own strength. God serves as their strong refuge whenever trouble surrounds them. Salvation is a gift of His free grace to all who depend on Him.

The Lord helps His people in times of deep distress and rescues them from the hands of the wicked. He saves them simply because they run to Him for shelter and trust in His care. Those who put their faith in God will never find their hope in vain.
